ranked.headline: Quantum learning models move beyond variational training toward scalable, trainable designs
ranked.summary: New preprints tackle exponential concentration, measurement-free Riemannian training, backprop-free quantum Transformers and transferable circuit search.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is making quantum learning models trainable and scalable without relying on standard variational gradient loops. One scheme performs Riemannian gradient optimization autonomously, without measurements or classical feedback. A fully quantum Transformer uses SVD-based non-unitary circuits and quantum nonlinear activations and is trained by multi-agent RL without backpropagation. On trainability, an empirical study of fidelity and projected quantum kernels and quantum extreme learning examines how entanglement, locality and bandwidth scaling govern exponential concentration. On expressivity, contractive layers add all-to-all couplings with one trainable parameter on Rydberg arrays. Architecture design is increasingly learned: LatentRL-QAS transfers circuit designs across qubit counts via latent-space RL, and an ML workflow extrapolates gate, measurement and reset syntax to scale holographic circuits. Adjacent work covers dephasing-based minimal quantum reservoirs, JEPA world models inferring Hamiltonian parameters, single-ancilla estimation of multi-time correlators, and a QCBM prior guiding classical network training. All are preprints.

ranked.headline: Displacement fields and stacking order tune valley, Berry curvature and Hall states
ranked.summary: New preprints on Bernal, rhombohedral and twisted graphene and TMD moiré bilayers map how gating and stacking select anomalous Hall and ordered phases.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control of band topology and valley/pseudospin order in graphene multilayers through displacement field, stacking sequence and twist. In ABA trilayer graphene, a displacement field inverts band edges, reverses Berry curvature and yields valley splitting. Bernal pentalayer experiments report displacement-field-tunable first-order transitions with hysteretic Hall responses, and Hartree-Fock work on Bernal tetralayer predicts interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and anomalous Hall metals. In 17-layer rhombohedral graphene, superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi pockets is enhanced by in-plane field. Twisted monolayer-N-layer rhombohedral graphene hosts narrow topological bands from Dirac-cone/surface-state hybridization tuned by layer number. Magic-angle twisted bilayer studies find hidden f-wave TIVC order near nu=-2, and Floquet driving is predicted to induce valley polarization. A parallel line addresses twisted TMDs: a microscopic, angle-independent continuum model and a non-quantized Chern metal in a holon model. All are preprints; no single mechanism spans these systems.

ranked.headline: Adaptive tensor, variational and quantum-assisted solvers push many-body dynamics further
ranked.summary: New preprints pair adaptive classical ansätze with quantum hardware data or early-FTQC algorithms to extend many-body dynamics and ground-state estimation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is algorithmic: making correlated quantum dynamics and ground-state problems tractable through adaptivity or hybrid quantum-classical input. On the classical side, multiset tree tensor networks with per-configuration bond-dimension adaptation yield converged exciton dynamics in Holstein-type models. An adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller scheme extends Hubbard quench dynamics to longer times and matches DMFT references across coupling strengths. Thermofield dynamics combined with ML-MCTDH and finite-basis Bogoliubov transforms handles anharmonic Morse baths for vibrational relaxation. For neural quantum states, an implicit-Euler stochastic reconfiguration underpins implicit augmented imaginary-time evolution. Hybrid approaches include Rydberg-array measurements used to pretrain RBM and RNN guiding wavefunctions for projective QMC, an early-FTQC algorithm estimating small energy differences such as molecular forces with lower sampling cost than phase estimation, and quantum-assisted ground-state estimation within simulated annealing to compress many-fermion bases.

ranked.headline: Combined probes test time-varying dark energy against ΛCDM and early-Universe extensions
ranked.summary: New HSC-Y3 shear, CMB+BAO recombination tests and scalar-tensor reconstructions probe the DESI-era preference for evolving dark energy.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether combined late- and early-Universe data prefer dynamical dark energy over ΛCDM. HSC-Y3 cosmic shear combined with DESI BAO, DES SNe and BBN priors yields a 2.4σ preference for a time-varying equation of state. Allowing w0wa removes the hinted early-recombination preference from CMB+BAO and gives the lowest AIC, suggesting the two extensions compete for the same data features. A genetic-algorithm reconstruction of scalar-tensor Lagrangians fit to DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, CMB and fσ8 improves on ΛCDM by Δχ²=-16.6. Systematics and early-Universe inputs are also being revisited: updated CMB acoustic priors separate early-Universe information from lensing and ISW, and DES supernova colour evolution constrains intergalactic dust that could shift distance moduli. Forecasts propose galaxy-CMB and galaxy-galaxy lensing ratios as geometric probes for LSST and Simons Observatory. Separately, axion early dark energy with JWST high-redshift galaxy abundances gives H0≈72.76 km/s/Mpc.

ranked.headline: Quantum circuits, cold atoms and classical methods target many-body and gauge dynamics
ranked.summary: New preprints pair quantum hardware encodings of gauge, light-matter and QCD cascades with improved classical solvers for spin, fermion and open-system dynamics.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is simulation of real-time many-body dynamics, split between quantum-hardware encodings and classical methods. On the quantum side, a cold-atom analog simulator of a 1D SU(2) quantum link model observes coherent meson-baryon conversion under tunable mass and gauge parameters. A Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson circuit evolves the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model and is benchmarked against exact diagonalization. A coherent quantum-circuit encoding of finite-state Mueller dipole branching at small x is compared with continuous cascades and H1 DIS data. On the classical side, cluster spin-LSC treats a sensor and strongly coupled bath spins quantum mechanically to model spin-qubit decoherence. Dirac propagation simulates local fermionic observables under particle-number-conserving unitaries. Transition path sampling is formulated for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion to extract rare-event rates. Separately, quantum Monte Carlo of 2D dipolar excitons yields an analytical framework for chemical potential and interaction energies.

ranked.headline: High-dimensional and nonclassical photon states are being generated, tailored and converted
ranked.summary: New preprints pair high-dimensional OAM and spatially entangled photon sources with squeezed-light and microwave biphoton schemes for tailored quantum light.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the generation and control of structured, high-dimensional or nonclassical light. Three preprints address spatial or OAM degrees of freedom: 128-dimensional single-photon OAM comb states with telecom-to-520 nm sum-frequency upconversion, phase-only hologram tailoring of OAM amplitude and phase, and a brighter high-dimensional spatially entangled pair source from beam-like Type-II SPDC in BBO with ~1.45x coincidence gain. Three further preprints are theoretical proposals built on other nonclassical resources: frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer, emitter scattering of squeezed vacuum for cat-cluster-state generation, and phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by coherent plus bright squeezed vacuum. The new element is the pairing of dimensionality scaling with source brightness and wavelength conversion, alongside squeezed-light and circuit-QED schemes. The previous emphasis on complete characterization is only weakly supported here.

ranked.headline: Decoders, compilers and simulators are co-designed for fault-tolerant quantum hardware
ranked.summary: New work targets the classical stack of fault-tolerant machines: microsecond GPU decoding, loss-aware decoders, verified compilers, speculation and trapped-ion QEC simulation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is classical software and control that must keep pace with, or resource-optimize, fault-tolerant quantum computation. On decoding, a GPU decoder for bivariate bicycle codes sustains one syndrome round per microsecond under circuit-level noise, and a loss-aware CNN decoder with a fast sampler reduces logical error rates for qubit loss in surface and high-rate qLDPC codes. On compilation, QBlue is extended to block-encoding algorithms with machine-checked verification, and LLM-driven search cuts the expected Toffoli count for RSA-2048 factoring by up to 78.6%. Froq adds safe speculative execution on live quantum states through recovery contracts, while THeatA models transport and heating in QCCD trapped-ion QEC. Hardware-aware and verifiable design is the common emphasis.

ranked.headline: Moiré superlattices tune polaritons and phonons in graphene; photonic metasurfaces show parallel BIC control
ranked.summary: Direct spectroscopic evidence of moiré-mediated coupling in graphene and graphene/hBN appears alongside metasurface studies of quasi-BIC and flatband tuning.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is moiré control of hybrid excitations in graphene-based systems. Twisted bilayer graphene, studied from AB stacking to 5.5°, hosts hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons with gate-tunable wavelengths via remote moiré effects. In graphene/hBN superlattices, a Fano resonance is reported as the first direct observation of coupling between moiré flat-band electronic excitations and hBN out-of-plane optical phonons. Helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy identifies reconfigurable chiral phonons in asymmetrically stacked moiré superlattices. Three metasurface works form a looser, parallel strand: THz collective flatbands with zero group velocity, polarization-independent strong coupling of Brillouin-zone-folding quasi-BICs with A excitons in WS2, and liquid-crystal tuning of anisotropy-induced quasi-BICs. The new element is direct spectroscopic evidence of moiré-mediated interlayer coupling alongside demonstrated tunability.

ranked.headline: Differentiable, GPU-accelerated forward models and automated fitting for survey inference
ranked.summary: Six preprints build and test systematics mitigation, emulators, forward models and automated lens fitting for SPHEREx, Euclid and 21-cm analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the engineering and validation of inference components for upcoming survey analyses. Two SPHEREx papers address the pipeline from both ends: an information-criterion-driven non-linear deprojection of angular imaging systematics, tested on lognormal mocks, and Hesperos and Eosphoros, a GPU-accelerated differentiable forced-photometry operator coupled to a forward model. A differentiable hybrid forward model for global 21-cm cosmology combines neural signal emulation with foreground parameterisation for uncertainty quantification. Emulator diagnostics appear in the Lyman-alpha work, where symbolic regression probes a GP emulator and a Sobolev loss improves derivative fidelity for most cases. Lens-Orchestra applies multimodal LLM agents to automate forward modeling of 185 Euclid Q1 lens candidates. The Popcorn Void Finder reimplementation documents the algorithm and reports a change in void size function from power-law to Schechter-like. The items span different observables and methods.

ranked.headline: Exact bounds on cost, reachability and convertibility under restricted quantum operations
ranked.summary: Five preprints quantify what restricted control, readout, randomness and free operations can achieve in quantum state and observable manipulation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is characterizing what a constrained set of operations can reach and at what cost. One preprint bounds the quantum-data copy cost of controlled amplitude amplification using no-signaling and distinguishability arguments, with quadratic scaling. Another studies reachability, geometry and preparation cost for multipartite states under differentiable collision-model control with partial-SWAP and Heisenberg exchange plus local phases. A third characterizes reachable effective observables of fixed-readout quantum neural networks under unitary, mixed-unitary and CPTP resources, with strict inclusions. A fourth shows eight labels suffice for interface choices in hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness. The fifth derives an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in quantum-state texture from a complete characterization of free operations. The new content is sharp, resource-specific boundaries rather than generic capability claims.

ranked.headline: Full-stack quantum workflows meet end-to-end cost estimates against classical baselines
ranked.summary: New stack and workflow papers appear alongside end-to-end estimates that test chemistry and ML advantage claims against classical methods and fault-tolerant targets.
ranked.synthesis: The current items shift from hardware-aware compilation per se to the surrounding software and cost-accounting layer. Cqlib offers a Rust-core stack with Python and C interfaces spanning simulation, compilation, algorithms, and QCIS hardware, while TyxonQ links QM/MM, fragment embedding, classical CCSD/FCI, and quantum solvers to MD engines for incremental quantum integration. The DOE blueprint sets a fault-tolerant target of 100+ logical qubits by 2028, scaling to 1,000-10,000. Two estimation papers temper advantage expectations: quantum linear solver training for linearized neural networks crosses over classically only at very large sizes, and SHCI/TrimCI benchmarks on 26 chemistry instances find classical computation cheaper for six of seven systems. The common thread is evaluating quantum workflows by end-to-end runtime and cost rather than abstract algorithmic scaling.

ranked.headline: Sharper error bounds and randomized methods for simulating Hamiltonians on quantum and classical hardware
ranked.summary: Five preprints tighten digitization and Trotter error control and probe classical simulability, sharpening resource estimates for Hamiltonian simulation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is quantifying and reducing approximation error in Hamiltonian simulation. For U(1) lattice gauge theory, a semiclassical analysis gives an improved digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates, sharpening qubit resource estimates. For Coulomb dynamics, Trotter and qDRIFT errors decay slowly because of the singularity; supersmoothing qDRIFT is introduced, with error linear in time. A phase-operator estimate of Trotter error, expressed through nested commutators, is reported as tighter than prior bounds for finite-size systems. Another paper finds Trotter errors in observables can be exponentially smaller for state 2-designs than 1-designs, quantified via frame potential. A classical free-probability algorithm for sparse random non-local Hamiltonians computes spectral fluctuations, thermal values and correlation functions, delimiting the quantum-classical boundary.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-defined orders predicted to yield tunable Hall and spin-transport responses
ranked.summary: Five preprints link symmetry-defined orders to predicted Hall and spin-transport responses, with electric-field or stacking tunability in several cases.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is theory deriving measurable transport responses from symmetry-defined order. For odd-parity magnets, charge-spin selection rules and temporal-spectral separation are proposed as general transport signatures. In monolayer H-phase MoS2, an orbital exchange field is shown to induce an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity without spin magnetism or spin-orbit coupling. Twisted bilayer NiPS3 is predicted to host p-wave spin textures that a perpendicular electric field reorients. Sliding antiferroelectric four-layer MoS2 is predicted to show a quantum-metric-driven nonlinear valley Hall effect, and axial ferrons in uniaxial ferroelectrics to show thermal and angular-momentum Hall effects. New here is the emphasis on orbital-only mechanisms and on electric-field or stacking tunability. All five items are preprints, with predictions from theory and first-principles calculations.

ranked.headline: Tools for halo modelling, N-body accuracy and SIDM resolution mature for Stage IV-era cosmology
ranked.summary: Four preprints advance halo occupation modelling, N-body validation, SIDM simulation and scalable supernova likelihoods for upcoming survey-scale analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure for connecting dark matter halo evolution to survey observables. SciPIC-lite supplies a public, flexible Halo Occupation Distribution pipeline aimed at clustering observables. PhotoNs-3 is tested against GADGET for accuracy and convergence in power spectra, halo profiles and mass functions, targeting Stage IV requirements. A separate N-body scheme for self-interacting dark matter uses distance-threshold interactions dependent on relative velocity and time step, aiming at enhanced spatial resolution and performance. The supernova Woodbury factorization paper is related mainly through scale: it reduces LSST-scale fit time from about 10 weeks to about 1.5 hr. Together, the items emphasize validated, computationally tractable pipelines rather than new halo-physics measurements.

ranked.headline: Foreground, calibration and birefringence systematics in CMB and 21 cm analyses are quantified
ranked.summary: Four preprints quantify CO foregrounds, polarization calibration and birefringence-induced lensing bias, plus 21 cm global-spectrum inference of cosmic dawn parameters.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is forward modeling of systematics and nuisance signals that can bias cosmological inference from CMB and 21 cm data. An analytic halo model for CO and CO×CIB finds a ~2σ parameter bias in CMB-HD-like settings. A Simons Observatory study examines transferring absolute polarization-angle calibration between LAT and SAT using simulations. Unmodeled anisotropic cosmic birefringence is shown to positively bias small-scale CMB lensing bandpowers, and joint MUSE estimation of lensing and birefringence is presented as a remedy. A fourth paper applies Bayesian inference to simulated DSL lunar-orbit 21 cm global spectra, combined with HERA/SKA-Low, to constrain cosmic dawn and reionization parameters. The FRB work in the previous synthesis is not supported by the current items.

ranked.headline: Electronic-structure models extended to long-range fields, strong correlation and exciton-phonon coupling
ranked.summary: Four preprints extend electronic-structure modeling to external fields, fictitious-temperature DFT, electron force fields and exciton-phonon workflows.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints extend electronic-structure descriptions beyond standard ground-state treatments, through learned models, reduced models, functional parameterization and workflow codes. MLEH-LR adds long-range interactions and external fields to a machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian, applied to boron nitride ribbons. The TAO-DFT work proposes a nonempirical, spin-symmetry-restoration scheme that sets a system-dependent fictitious temperature for lowest singlet states of molecules. LeIFF represents valence electrons as dynamical spherical charge distributions in a compact force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics at large scale. LetzElPhC is an open-source code that computes electron-phonon and exciton-phonon matrix elements from Quantum ESPRESSO DFPT output and interfaces with Yambo. The common thread is expanded physical scope, with fields, correlation, coupled dynamics and exciton-phonon coupling, at controlled computational cost.

ranked.headline: Field-level mappings extend simulations to Lyα flux, dark energy and scalar-field dark matter
ranked.summary: Four preprints validate field-level shortcuts against reference simulations for Lyα mocks, dark energy matching and scalar-field dark matter initial conditions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is extending expensive simulations through field-level mappings checked against reference runs. A 3D U-Net maps density and velocity fields to Lyman-alpha flux, reproducing P1D, bispectrum and trispectrum across IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO. Two papers argue that N-body dynamics depend only on the expansion history a(τ), so constant-w simulations can reproduce CPL and more general w(z) models; one reports agreement within 0.2% in power. A fourth develops matched LCDM-SFDM initial conditions linking CLASS-SFDM, MUSIC and AxioNyx, and finds that accurate density recovery does not ensure adequate wave-phase resolution. The scalar-field dark matter initial-condition validation is new relative to the prior synthesis, which also cited a CAMELS gas emulator and a DESI-BGS assembly-bias test; neither appears among the current items.

ranked.headline: Wide-field spectroscopy and lensing map structure and its baryons from protoclusters to cosmic noon
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 preprints apply DESI, HSC-SSP and JWST data to protoclusters, cluster lenses, group baryons and Little Red Dot demographics.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is survey-based mapping of structure and its tracers across cosmic time, not a dark-energy test. DESI DR1 physical quasar pairs at z≈2, with separations up to 2.5 Mpc, trace protocluster environments consistent with ΛCDM mock predictions. VENUS supplies strong-lensing models for 57 JWST clusters with 1733 multiply-imaged systems and derives mass scaling relations. Localized FRBs crossmatched with DESI galaxy groups give a tentative 143 pc cm^-3 excess dispersion measure for group-intersecting sight lines, a low-significance baryon probe. An HSC-SSP spectroscopic search finds the Little Red Dot number density falling ~35x from z~4-8 to z~2.1-2.6 while the luminosity-function knee does not evolve. The items differ in tracer and scale; the shared element is large-area survey data.

ranked.headline: Hybrid bias expansions extend to reconstructed clustering, baryons and PNG bias priors
ranked.summary: Four preprints extend hybrid bias modelling to reconstruction, baryons and PNG bias, supporting analyses of upcoming galaxy surveys.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of simulation-informed, hybrid descriptions of tracer and gas bias in large-scale-structure analyses. A hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion is extended to post-reconstruction galaxy clustering, where a combined pre- and post-reconstruction analysis improves cosmological constraints. A hybrid effective field theory for diffuse baryons combines N-body displacements, a Lorentzian feedback suppression and linear bias. For primordial non-Gaussianity, a flexible subhalo abundance matching model fit to small-scale clustering, together with separate-universe simulations, constrains the bias parameter b_φ. CosmoMap, a conditioned 3D U-Net, differs in method, predicting hot gas temperature and electron density from dark matter fields in CAMELS IllustrisTNG. Together, these works pair simulation inputs with compact bias parameterisations.

ranked.headline: Space-time metasurfaces program polarization topology and coherence in classical wavepackets
ranked.summary: Four preprints show spatiotemporal metasurfaces and vectorial wavepackets encoding knots, toroidal pulses, quantum-inspired bits and entanglement analogues in classical fields.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is spatiotemporal structure used as a programmable degree of freedom in classical electromagnetic fields, with polarization as the principal carrier. One preprint builds vectorial wavepackets whose Stokes trajectories form linked and knotted topologies. Another uses a graphene optoelectronic metasurface to generate and tune toroidal terahertz pulses through transient vectorial photocurrents. Two space-time metasurface works program coherence: one synthesizes polarization states into quantum-inspired bits across 48 resolved channels, and the other realizes Bell- and GHZ-like multipartite states. The terahertz work shares the vectorial-topology theme but uses a different generation route. What is new is the move from static polarization topology toward joint, explicit control of topology, coherence and temporal structure within classical light.

ranked.headline: Coded, holographic and speckle methods recover wavefronts in disordered media
ranked.summary: November 2026 preprints add phase-coded, holographic and deep-learning routes to wavefront recovery through disordered or turbulent media.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is recovering wavefront information in disordered or turbulent optical systems, where spatially varying phase and a field-dependent point-spread function complicate conventional reconstruction. The anisoplanatic blind deconvolution preprint uses a pupil-plane spatial light modulator with known phase codes to jointly recover the image and spatially varying turbulence phases. The holographic-gradient preprint instead obtains the loss gradient from a single off-axis hologram, enabling in situ training of optical systems through disorder. The deep-learning preprint reconstructs multiple wavefronts from one speckle pattern produced by a thin diffuser, using recurrent all-pairs field transforms and Zernike regression. Two of the three preprints rely on single-shot or single-pattern acquisition. All three are preprints, and no quantitative comparison between them is presented here.

ranked.headline: Baryonic effects, mass calibration and gamma-ray forecasts probe dark matter structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that baryons and survey depth now govern the sensitivity of dark matter lensing, annihilation and mass-calibration tests.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a common concern: how baryonic physics and observational calibration limit the use of galaxy-scale and cluster-scale structure as probes of dark matter. Baryon-enhanced strong lensing shows that compact baryons make galaxy-hosting self-interacting dark matter subhalos stronger lenses than CDM, with GGSL cross sections 1.4-2.7 times CDM in TNG300-1. The gamma-ray forecast for Milky Way dwarf galaxies finds LSST gains to be modest, with high-J-factor satellites dominating sensitivity. The joint DES and SPT framework combines optical richness and weak lensing with Sunyaev-Zel'dovich signals to calibrate cluster masses. These works address distinct systems and do not form a single analysis, but each quantifies how the interpretation of an observable depends on modeling choices and calibration.

ranked.headline: Stacking and geometry tune nonlinear transport, magnetism and excitons in 2D systems
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints link band geometry, lattice stacking and edge effects to transport and optical selection rules in 2D platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share an emphasis on geometry and symmetry controlling response in two-dimensional electronic systems, not on disorder. arxiv:2611.28213 is a tight-binding study of quantum-geometric nonlinear conductivity in SrTiO3 two-dimensional electron gases, comparing (001) and (111) interfaces, with multiorbital driving as the reported mechanism. arxiv:2611.30343 examines electronic and magnetic states in semi-Dirac quantum dots, where triangular and hexagonal geometries yield edge-asymmetric magnetism. arxiv:2611.34900 reports that rhombohedral stacking in 3R-MoS2 bilayers brightens spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons, identified through g-factors and resonant hybridization. Across the set, the new element is the explicit link between geometric or stacking choices and responses that are otherwise suppressed. The methods and observables differ, so the shared thread is geometry-controlled response rather than a common mechanism.

ranked.headline: Metasurface design limits for polarization-resolved beam and Jones-matrix control
ranked.summary: Three November 2026 preprints advance inverse design and analytical bounds for polarization-controlling metasurfaces.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the design of metasurfaces and metagratings that control the polarization state of transmitted or diffracted light. Three preprints approach this from different directions. arXiv:2611.27311 applies analytical mode-matching to dielectric-loaded perforated metallic metagratings that provide dual-polarized anomalous refraction. arXiv:2611.28364 introduces a differentiable topology optimization framework for polarization-analyzing gratings and explicitly removes the paraxial restriction of the Jones-Fourier formalism. arXiv:2611.34146 derives analytically tractable minimum effective-susceptibility bounds for metasurfaces realizing unitary and nonunitary Jones polarization transformations. The items do not share a single methodology. The common element is Jones-level control of polarization in metasurfaces, pursued through both numerical inverse design and analytical limits on material response.

ranked.headline: Dissipative soliton generation and dynamics in microresonators and fiber lasers
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints address turnkey soliton start-up, pulse-to-pulse dispersion control, and soliton dynamics in fiber lasers.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is dissipative soliton dynamics, in which localized pulses or states are sustained by a balance of dispersion, Kerr nonlinearity, gain or loss, and external driving. One preprint analyzes turnkey dissipative Kerr soliton generation in self-injection-locked photonic-crystal ring resonators using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations. A second introduces dissipative erasure, a spectral-filtering and nonlinear-amplification scheme that removes pulse-to-pulse dispersion imbalance in burst-mode ultrafast lasers. A survey chapter reviews temporal solitons in mode-locked fiber lasers, including soliton molecules and dispersion-managed solitons. The items are heterogeneous: the first two are research contributions on different platforms, while the third is a review. What is new is the explicit treatment of turnkey start-up in photonic-crystal microresonators and a spectral-filtering route to dispersion-imbalance removal in burst-mode lasers.

ranked.headline: Nonadiabatic tunneling and blueshifted harmonics in driven correlated insulators
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report nonadiabatic tunneling in NiPS3 and non-integer high harmonics in Sr2CuO3 under optical driving, alongside broadband THz methods.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a focus on the nonadiabatic response of correlated insulators to light fields. The NiPS3 study uses time-resolved optical spectroscopy to report nonadiabatic quantum tunneling and ponderomotive blue-shifted resonances near the Keldysh regime. The Sr2CuO3 work, combining experiment and simulation, reports non-integer, blueshifted high harmonic generation under mid-infrared driving, attributed to many-body nonadiabatic gating. The Yb-laser terahertz platform is methodological, pairing multi-pass-cell compression, spintronic THz generation and air-biased detection over a broad bandwidth, a route suited to such nonequilibrium measurements. What is new in these items is the joint treatment of tunneling and harmonic response in driven correlated insulators, probed with broadband, high-sensitivity techniques.

ranked.headline: Gain-loss balance and nonreciprocal coupling steer non-Hermitian spectral structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints map distinct gain-loss and nonreciprocal coupling mechanisms that control non-Hermitian eigenstate and symmetry structure.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of gain-loss balance and coupling asymmetry as handles on non-Hermitian spectral structure. One preprint shows that, in time-dependent T-symmetric systems with gain and loss, gain-loss induced symmetry breaking is forbidden even for random gain-loss distributions, which constrains what such control can achieve. Another introduces pseudo-altermagnetism, in which balanced gain and loss mimic altermagnetic spin splitting, with movable nodal structures. A third shows that tunable nonreciprocal coupling near a second-order polarization exceptional point produces state-selective eigenstate splitting, with one branch distinguished. The items are heterogeneous: the first establishes a constraint, while the other two describe control mechanisms. What is new is the specific set of mechanisms and constraints rather than a single unified result.

ranked.headline: Physics-informed networks embedding wave propagation in optical inverse problems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend physics-informed learning to diffractive design, diffraction tomography and high-harmonic spectroscopy analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the embedding of explicit physics into learned models for optical inverse problems. MSWNets couple fully connected networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation in a PINN-inspired formulation to design broadband diffractive optics. Gradient optical diffraction tomography uses physics-informed deep learning, with a ResNet, to estimate the missing amplitude gradient, extending gradient-based tomography to amplitude retrieval. Across these two diffractive items, what is new is that propagation physics is built into the learning or estimation step itself. The AI-assisted topological high-harmonic study retrieves anisotropic nonlinear responses and crystal symmetries of atomically thin materials; it shares only the learning-for-inference element and addresses a different nonlinear light-matter regime.

ranked.headline: Engineering nonlinear and PT-symmetric control in driven coupled cavities
ranked.summary: Theoretical cavity proposals treat nonlinearity, asymmetric dissipation, Floquet driving, and PT symmetry as explicit control parameters.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a common thread: engineering coherent control in driven, coupled cavity systems by tailoring nonlinear terms, dissipation, or sideband driving. The first derives analytic optimal conditions for unconventional photon blockade in coupled cavities with second-order nonlinearity and asymmetric dissipation, targeting robust antibunching. The second proposes a Floquet sideband method to manipulate mechanical dark modes in a three-mode optomechanical system, supported by fidelity and population analyses. The third applies PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics, using second-order sidebands and tunable slow-fast light, to magnetometry with theoretical picotesla-level sensitivity. What is new in each case is the explicit use of nonlinearity, asymmetric dissipation, Floquet driving, or PT symmetry as control parameters. All listed works are theoretical, and their summaries report no experimental validation.

ranked.headline: Lattice topological phases classified by generalized protecting symmetries and invariants
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend symmetry-constrained classification of lattice topological phases to half-chiral symmetry, spin space groups and fractal lattices.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is symmetry-constrained classification: the controlling symmetry, invariant or lattice setting is widened, and the resulting phases or magnetic orders are then enumerated or characterized accordingly. One preprint identifies topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry, in which chiral symmetry acts on a single sublattice, and characterizes them with real-space invariants and zero-energy modes. A second enumerates spin space groups via translation holonomy, yielding 17 spin-lattice types with neutron diffraction signatures; this is a classification of magnetic order rather than a topological-phase study. A third realizes SSH, Haldane, Qi-Wu-Zhang and Z2 insulators on fractal lattices, including site-eliminated, projected and patterned constructions, transferring established models to new geometries. What is new is the extension of protecting symmetries, invariants and lattice geometries, rather than a single shared method.

ranked.headline: Josephson and superconducting proposals for noise, thermometry and spin conversion
ranked.summary: Recent preprints propose superconducting and Josephson devices whose design predictions target thermal noise, thermometry and spin-to-charge conversion.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is phase-coherent control of charge, spin and thermal responses by superconducting or Josephson elements. A numerical study proposes a flux-driven DC-SQUID threshold detector whose nonequilibrium phase dynamics aim to reduce thermal noise while detecting microwave pulses near the single-microwave-photon energy scale. A theory proposal for a two-orbital quantum dot Josephson junction with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting maps a temperature difference onto a phase difference for thermometry. A third preprint argues that the inverse spin Hall effect in a superconductor could approach unity spin-to-charge conversion in a nonlocal spin-valve geometry. All three items are theoretical or numerical proposals, so the new content consists of design predictions rather than experimental demonstrations.

ranked.headline: Physics-Trained Surrogates for Optical Imaging Design and Blind Deconvolution
ranked.summary: Simulation-trained surrogates now link physical models to optical design and blind PSF estimation in these preprints.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a reliance on physics-based simulation to train or guide learned models for optical systems, although their roles differ. A surrogate-guided design of incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks targets onboard satellite image classification, treating the optical hardware as a design variable rather than a reconstruction problem. A neural surrogate for scintillator light-guide photon transport, trained via adjoint Monte Carlo sampling, makes detector readout differentiable so that geometry and readout can be co-optimized. DeepBlur, trained on physical simulations, addresses the inverse problem instead, estimating spatially varying 2D point spread functions blindly from single microscopy images to improve deconvolution. What is new across the set is the use of differentiable or simulation-trained surrogates to couple forward physics with either design or inference, rather than a single shared modality. The dominant thread is therefore the surrogate-mediated coupling of physical models to computational optical imaging, not a common instrument.
